newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SKB bank says 1996 net up 2.5 times.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SKB bank says 1996 net up 2.5 times.

text.p: Slovenia's second largest bank SKB said its 1996 net profit rose to 1.48 billion tolars ($9.6 million) from 602 million tolars a year earlier.
The bank said the gain in earnings was powered by improved interest margins as well as an expansion of both retail and wholesale business.

"The biggest increase (in operations) was recorded in the area of loans to individuals which were up 23 percent, while financial cross-border transactions rose by seven percent," chief executive Ivan Nerad told a news conference.
SKB's total assets rose 15 percent to 206.8 billion tolars ($1.3 billion), exceeding the bank's own forecast of an eight percent increase.
"We improved the quality of our balance sheet last year and and opened six new branches in Slovenia, taking the total number of branches to 54," Nerad added.

He said the bank had not yet decided on its 1996 dividend, but that he expected it to be "slightly higher" than the 1,100 tolars per share paid in 1995. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom +386-61 125 8439
